title: Constructible finite-coefficient sheaves on an oriented product
statement: Let $a:X\to S$ and $b:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Put $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$, the left oriented product of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. A sheaf $F$ of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_P$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is called constructible if there are finite stratifications $X=\coprod_\alpha X_\alpha$, $Y=\coprod_\beta Y_\beta$ [def-constructible-stratification], with each stratum constructible as a subset [def-weil-constructible-subset], such that each restriction to $P_{\alpha\beta}=(X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(Y_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ is locally constant with finite $\Lambda$-module values. The map $P_{\alpha\beta}\to P$ is the morphism given by [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] from the projections, the stratum immersions, and the oriented $2$-morphism. Restriction is inverse image along that map. Here locally constant with finite values means that there is a covering family $(U_i)$ of the final object of $P_{\alpha\beta}$ such that on the slice topos $P_{\alpha\beta}/U_i$ the restricted sheaf is isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline{M_i}$ for a $\Lambda$-module $M_i$ finite as a set. For $Y=S$ and $b=1_S$, this defines constructibility on the vanishing topos $V_a$ [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].

source.place: Definition immediately following Theorem 4.27, printed p. 37, specialized to finite Lambda; for general oriented products compare Orgogozo author draft, Section 8.1 (printed p. 17), which explicitly extends the finite-partition definition of Theorem 7.1 to X left-oriented-product_Y Z.
